extracted.intended_audience: NIH grant applicants and recipients (PD/PIs, AORs, research administrators, grants management staff)
extracted.subtask_description: Policy and procedural standards from the NIH Grants Policy Statement covering definitions, roles and responsibilities, cost and award administration, eRA Commons registration requirements, and other terms and conditions relevant to preparing, submitting, managing, and auditing NIH grants.

rubrics_metrics.name: Questioned costs — calculation and scope
rubrics_metrics.description: The questioned cost amount is calculated as if the portion of a transaction that lacked adequate documentation were confirmed non-compliant.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Questioned costs are developed by the auditor and reflect amounts lacking adequate documentation; see distinctions for known vs. likely questioned costs.

rubrics_metrics.name: When a cost is not a questioned cost
rubrics_metrics.description: There is no questioned cost solely because of: (i) deficiencies in internal control; or (ii) noncompliance with the reporting type of compliance requirement if this noncompliance does not affect the amount expended or received from the Federal award.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Deficiencies or reporting noncompliance alone do not create a questioned cost unless they affect the dollar amount.

rubrics_metrics.name: Known questioned cost
rubrics_metrics.description: Known questioned cost means a questioned cost specifically identified by the auditor; known questioned costs are a subset of likely questioned costs.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Used when the auditor can specifically identify noncompliant amounts in the audit evidence.

rubrics_metrics.name: Likely questioned cost — auditor extrapolation
rubrics_metrics.description: Likely questioned cost means the auditor’s best estimate of total questioned costs, developed by extrapolating from audit evidence (for example, projecting known questioned costs identified in an audit sample to the entire population).
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Auditors consider likely questioned costs when evaluating effect on the opinion on compliance.

rubrics_metrics.name: Questioned costs vs improper payments
rubrics_metrics.description: Questioned costs are not improper payments until reviewed and confirmed to be improper payments as defined in OMB Circular A–123 Appendix C.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Separate processes determine whether a questioned cost becomes an improper payment.

rubrics_metrics.name: Real property definition
rubrics_metrics.description: Real property: Land, including land improvements, structures and appurtenances thereto, and legal interests in land (fee interest, licenses, rights of way, easements).
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Real property excludes moveable machinery and equipment.

rubrics_metrics.name: Recipient definition
rubrics_metrics.description: Recipient: An entity that receives a Federal award directly from a Federal agency to carry out an activity under a Federal program; does not include subrecipients, consortiums, or individuals that are participants or beneficiaries.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: See also Non-Federal entity for related distinctions.

rubrics_metrics.name: Renewal application requirements
rubrics_metrics.description: Renewal application: An application requesting additional funding for a period subsequent to that provided by a current award; must be developed as fully as though applying for the first time and competes with all other peer reviewed applications.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Previous NIH term was 'competing continuation.'

rubrics_metrics.name: Renewal award definition
rubrics_metrics.description: Renewal award: A Federal award with a start date contiguous with, or closely following, the end of the expiring award; the start date begins a new and distinct period of performance.

rubrics_metrics.name: Research & Development (R&D) definition
rubrics_metrics.description: R&D includes all basic and applied research activities and all development activities performed by HHS award recipients; includes research training activities that use the same facilities as other R&D activities and are not part of instruction.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Research = systematic study for fuller scientific knowledge; Development = use of knowledge from research to produce useful materials/systems/methods including prototypes.

rubrics_metrics.name: Research Administrator role
rubrics_metrics.description: Research Administrator: Acts as a local agent of the AOR and/or PD/PIs providing day-to-day grant-related support.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Can be centrally located or within a department; supports administrative tasks but NIH conducts official business only with designated PD/PIs and AORs.

rubrics_metrics.name: Research misconduct definition and components
rubrics_metrics.description: Research misconduct means fabrication, falsification, or plagiarism in proposing, performing, reviewing, or reporting research results.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Fabrication = making up data/results; Falsification = manipulating materials/equipment/processes or changing/omitting data so research is not accurately represented; Plagiarism = appropriation of another’s ideas/processes/results/words without appropriate credit. Research misconduct does not include honest error or honest differences of opinion.

rubrics_metrics.name: Research patient care costs
rubrics_metrics.description: Research patient care costs: Costs of routine and ancillary services provided by hospitals to participants in research protocols.

rubrics_metrics.name: Responsible party (ClinicalTrials.gov) definition
rubrics_metrics.description: Responsible party: Term used in FDAAA to refer to the entity or individual responsible under FDAAA for registering a clinical trial and submitting clinical trial information to ClinicalTrials.gov.

rubrics_metrics.name: Resubmission application policy
rubrics_metrics.description: Resubmission application: An application previously submitted but not funded and being resubmitted for new consideration; applicants must make significant changes and can only resubmit once (suffix A1).
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Applicants must apply and undergo peer review; additional policies in Application Instruction Guide.

rubrics_metrics.name: Revision application (NIH 'revision')
rubrics_metrics.description: Revision application (as defined in SF424 (R&R)): Proposes a change in (1) the Federal Government’s financial obligations or contingent liability from an existing obligation, or (2) other change in terms and conditions of the existing award; NIH uses revision (S1) to request increase in current budget period for expansion of scope or protocol.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Applicants must apply and undergo peer review; NIH note: former NIH term 'revision' is now 'resubmission' for submitted-but-not-funded applications.

rubrics_metrics.name: Scientific data definition — included/excluded
rubrics_metrics.description: Scientific Data: Recorded factual material commonly accepted in the scientific community as of sufficient quality to validate and replicate research findings.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Does not include laboratory notebooks, preliminary analyses, completed case report forms, drafts, plans for future research, peer reviews, communications with colleagues, or physical objects such as specimens.

rubrics_metrics.name: Scientific Review Group (SRG) composition rule
rubrics_metrics.description: SRG: A peer review committee group of primarily non-government experts; no more than one-fourth of SRG members may be Federal employees (per 42 CFR Part 52(h)).
rubrics_metrics.guidance: SROs manage SRG activities; SRG evaluates scientific and technical merit.

rubrics_metrics.name: Scientific Review Officer (SRO) responsibilities
rubrics_metrics.description: SRO: NIH official who manages SRG activities, ensures compliance with laws/policies, reviews applications for completeness/conformity, ensures adequate reviewer expertise, assigns reviewers and discussion leaders, manages conflicts of interest and confidentiality, and serves as applicant point of contact during initial peer review phase.

rubrics_metrics.name: Scope of work definition
rubrics_metrics.description: Scope of work: The aims, objectives, purposes of a grant and the methodology, approach, analyses, tools, technologies, and timeframes needed to meet the grant’s objectives; includes research/training plan and approved modifications.

rubrics_metrics.name: Senior/Key Personnel involvement requirement
rubrics_metrics.description: Senior/Key Personnel: PD/PI and others who contribute substantively to scientific development or execution must devote measurable effort to the project; 'zero percent' or 'as needed' are not acceptable levels for those designated as Senior/Key Personnel.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Can include doctoral, masters, baccalaureate-level individuals, consultants, and postdocs if involvement is substantive and measurable.

rubrics_metrics.name: Significant rebudgeting threshold
rubrics_metrics.description: Significant rebudgeting: A threshold reached when expenditures in a single direct cost budget category deviate (increase or decrease) from the categorical commitment level established for the budget period by more than 25 percent of the total costs awarded.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Significant rebudgeting is one indicator of change in scope.

rubrics_metrics.name: Simplified acquisition threshold / small purchase methods
rubrics_metrics.description: Simplified acquisition threshold: The dollar amount below which a recipient or subrecipient may purchase property or services using small purchase methods as set by the Federal Acquisition Regulation (48 CFR Subpart 2.1).
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Recipients adopt small purchase procedures to expedite purchases below this threshold; see Micro-purchase for related rules.

rubrics_metrics.name: Small business concern definition
rubrics_metrics.description: Small business concern: Independently owned/operated for-profit business not dominant in its field, principal place in U.S., at least 51% U.S. citizen or lawful permanent resident ownership (or 51% voting stock), with affiliates combined having not more than 500 employees, and meeting SBA regulatory requirements (13 CFR Part 121).

rubrics_metrics.name: Special purpose equipment definition
rubrics_metrics.description: Special purpose equipment: Equipment used only for research, medical, scientific, or other similar technical activities (examples: microscopes, x-ray machines, surgical instruments, spectrometers and associated software).
rubrics_metrics.guidance: See also general Equipment definitions for capitalization and other rules.

rubrics_metrics.name: State and State government definitions for NIH grants
rubrics_metrics.description: State: Any U.S. state, DC, Puerto Rico, U.S. Virgin Islands, Guam, American Samoa, Northern Mariana Islands, and agencies/instrumentalities thereof (exclusive of local governments). State government: Government of any State or agency/instrumentality thereof (exclusive of local governments); federally recognized Indian tribal governments generally considered State governments for NIH grants.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: State institutions of higher education and State hospitals are not considered State governments for HHS general administrative requirements.

rubrics_metrics.name: Stipend — fellowship payment nature
rubrics_metrics.description: Stipend: A payment made to an individual under a fellowship or training grant according to pre-established levels to provide for living expenses during training; a stipend is not considered compensation for services expected of an employee.

rubrics_metrics.name: Subaward — definition and required form
rubrics_metrics.description: Subaward: An award provided by a pass-through entity to a subrecipient for the subrecipient to contribute to the goals/objectives of the project by carrying out part of a Federal award; does not include payments to a contractor, beneficiary, or participant.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: A subaward may be provided through any legal agreement consistent with criteria in 2 CFR Part 200.331, including consortium agreements; the recipient must enter into a formal written agreement signed by both parties (see Chapter 15).

rubrics_metrics.name: Subrecipient definition
rubrics_metrics.description: Subrecipient: A non-Federal entity that receives a subaward from a pass-through entity to carry out part of a Federal award; does not include a beneficiary or participant; may also be a direct recipient of other Federal awards.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Term includes consortium participants.

rubrics_metrics.name: Subsidiary definition
rubrics_metrics.description: Subsidiary: An entity in which more than 50 percent is owned or controlled directly by a parent corporation or through another subsidiary of a parent corporation.

rubrics_metrics.name: Successor-in-interest (SII) definition and effect
rubrics_metrics.description: Successor-in-interest: Process whereby rights to and obligations under NIH grants are acquired incidental to transfer of all assets or part of assets involved in performance of the grant(s); may result from legislative or legal action such as merger or corporate change.

rubrics_metrics.name: Supply definition and computing device rule
rubrics_metrics.description: Supply: All tangible personal property other than Equipment. A computing device is a supply if acquisition cost is below the lesser of the recipient’s capitalization level or $10,000, regardless of useful life.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: See Computing devices and Equipment for additional distinctions.

rubrics_metrics.name: Suspension of award activities (NIH action)
rubrics_metrics.description: Suspension of award activities: An action by the NIH awarding IC requiring the recipient to cease all activities on the award pending corrective action by the recipient; separate from suspension under HHS debarment/suspension regulations.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: See Public Policy Requirements (Debarment and Suspension) and Administrative Requirements—Enforcement Actions.

rubrics_metrics.name: Termination definition (agency action)
rubrics_metrics.description: Termination: The action a Federal agency or pass-through entity takes to discontinue a Federal award, in whole or in part, at any time before the planned end date; does not include discontinuing due to lack of available funds.

rubrics_metrics.name: Terms and conditions of award — scope
rubrics_metrics.description: Terms and conditions of award: All legal requirements imposed on a grant by NIH, whether based on statute, regulation, policy, or other referenced document, or specified by the grant award document itself; the NoA may include standard and specific award conditions necessary to attain objectives, facilitate administration, conserve funds, or protect the Federal government’s interests.

rubrics_metrics.name: Third-party in-kind contributions
rubrics_metrics.description: Third-party in-kind contributions: Value of non-cash contributions (property or services) that (1) benefit a project funded by a Federal award and (2) are contributed by non-Federal third parties without charge to a non-Federal entity under a Federal award.

rubrics_metrics.name: Total costs definition
rubrics_metrics.description: Total costs: The total allowable costs (direct and indirect) incurred by the recipient to carry out a grant-supported project or activity; includes costs charged to the NIH grant and costs borne by the recipient to satisfy matching or cost-sharing requirements.

rubrics_metrics.name: Uniform Administrative Requirements (Uniform Guidance)
rubrics_metrics.description: Uniform Guidance: The administrative requirements, cost principles and audit requirements for Federal awards to non-Federal entities as set forth in 2 CFR Part 200.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Also referred to as 'Uniform Guidance'.

rubrics_metrics.name: Unique Entity Identifier (UEI)
rubrics_metrics.description: UEI: The identifier assigned by the System for Award Management (SAM) to uniquely identify business entities.

rubrics_metrics.name: United States (definition for NIH purposes)
rubrics_metrics.description: United States: The 50 States, territories, and possessions of the United States, the Commonwealth of Puerto Rico, the Trust Territory of the Pacific Islands, and the District of Columbia.

rubrics_metrics.name: Unliquidated obligations
rubrics_metrics.description: Unliquidated obligations: Financial obligations incurred by the recipient or subrecipient but not paid (liquidated) for reports prepared on a cash basis; for accrual basis, obligations incurred but for which expenditures have not been recorded.

rubrics_metrics.name: Unobligated balance
rubrics_metrics.description: Unobligated balance: The amount of funds authorized under a Federal award that the recipient or subrecipient has not obligated, computed by subtracting cumulative unliquidated obligations and expenditures from the cumulative amount authorized to obligate.

rubrics_metrics.name: U.S. Person definition
rubrics_metrics.description: U.S. Person: Any U.S. citizen, national, lawful permanent resident; refugee or asylee admitted/granted asylum under specified U.S. statutes; any entity organized solely under U.S. laws (including foreign branches); or any person in the United States (per 28 CFR § 202.256).

rubrics_metrics.name: Withholding of support
rubrics_metrics.description: Withholding of support: A decision by NIH not to make a non-competing continuation award within the current competitive segment.

rubrics_metrics.name: Grants Management Officer (GMO) responsibilities
rubrics_metrics.description: GMO: NIH official (named in the NoA) responsible for business management and non-programmatic aspects of the award, including evaluating administrative content and compliance, negotiating grants, providing consultation/technical assistance, interpreting grants administration policies, administering and closing out grants, acting on requests for NIH prior approval or changes to terms/conditions, and being the only NIH official authorized to obligate funds or change funding/duration/terms of award.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: GMO works closely with Program Official (PO) and is focal point for prior approval requests; Chief Grants Management Officer provides leadership and appoints GMOs.

rubrics_metrics.name: Grants Management Specialist (GMS) role
rubrics_metrics.description: GMS: An agent of the GMO named in the NoA and assigned responsibility for day-to-day management of a portfolio of grants.

rubrics_metrics.name: Program Official (PO) responsibilities
rubrics_metrics.description: PO: Responsible for programmatic, scientific, and/or technical aspects of assigned applications and grants; duties include development of research/training programs, coordination with CSR/IC SROs, post-award administration such as review of progress reports and site visits, and working as a team with the GMO.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: PO handles scientific aspects while GMO handles business/administrative aspects.

rubrics_metrics.name: Other NIH/HHS staff specialized roles
rubrics_metrics.description: Other staff (e.g., offices negotiating indirect costs, ONR, DFAS, OIG, OHRP, ORI, OLAW, OPERA) coordinate with GMO but are responsible for discrete specialized areas and are not required to channel communications through the GMO.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Part III lists these organizations and contact information.

rubrics_metrics.name: Authorized Organization Representative (AOR) duties and certifications
rubrics_metrics.description: AOR: Designated representative of the recipient organization for award and administration matters; must ascertain that application materials submitted on behalf of the PD/PI are the PD/PI’s original work, certify compliance with required assurances and certifications, and certify organizational accountability for appropriate use of funds and performance of the project; holds the Signing Official role in eRA Commons.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: For electronic submissions the AOR signature is authenticated through Grants.gov registration; NIH requires designation of such an official but does not specify organizational location.

rubrics_metrics.name: Program Director/Principal Investigator (PD/PI) authorities and responsibilities
rubrics_metrics.description: PD/PI: Individual designated by applicant organization with authority/responsibility to direct the project; accountable for proper conduct of the project including submission of required reports; may be multiple PD/PIs sharing authority and responsibility; presence of multiple PD/PIs does not diminish individual responsibility/accountability.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: If single PD/PI is not an employee, organization must have a formal written agreement specifying the relationship; NIH will assess whether arrangement allows fulfillment of responsibilities if PD/PI is not an employee.

rubrics_metrics.name: Multiple PD/PI and Contact PD/PI requirements
rubrics_metrics.description: When multiple PD/PIs are designated NIH requires identification of one Contact PD/PI responsible for communication between PD/PIs and NIH; Contact PD/PI must meet all eligibility requirements and be affiliated with the applicant organization; Contact designation confers no special authorities within the project team.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: When PD/PIs are at different organizations only the Contact PD/PI must have the official relationship with the applicant organization; PD/PIs at other organizations must have a documented relationship with a consortium organization.

rubrics_metrics.name: PD/PI administrative/accountability collaboration with institutional staff
rubrics_metrics.description: PD/PIs are responsible for ensuring compliance with financial and administrative aspects of the award and work closely with designated institutional officials to create/maintain necessary documentation, submit justifications, acknowledge Federal support in publications/media, and ensure compliance with Federal and organizational requirements.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: NIH encourages PD/PIs to maintain contact with NIH PO for scientific aspects and GMO/GMS for business/administrative aspects.

rubrics_metrics.name: eRA Commons registration requirement for organizations
rubrics_metrics.description: An organization must complete one-time registration in the eRA Commons; institutional/organizational officials are responsible for registering PD/PIs. Organizations should allow 2–4 weeks to complete registration.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Prospective applicants should consult Legal Implications of Applications before beginning registration; NIH may preliminarily assess applicant eligibility during registration and may deny registration if ineligible.

rubrics_metrics.name: eRA Commons registration for PD/PI — role and affiliation
rubrics_metrics.description: PD/PI(s) designated on the application must be registered in eRA Commons, hold a PI eRA Commons role, and be affiliated with the applicant organization; initial registration must be done by an AOR with SO role or other authorized account administrators.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: PI role provides administrative authority to view summary statements, scores, submission status, and to complete post-award actions; users should have only one PD/PI eRA Commons account; if already registered by another organization, affiliate the individual with the submitting organization so they can view records.

rubrics_metrics.name: eRA Commons registration for undergraduate/graduate/postdoctoral participants
rubrics_metrics.description: Any individual with an Undergraduate, Graduate Student, and/or Postdoctoral Role who participates in an NIH-funded project for at least one person-month should be registered in eRA Commons and verify personal profile information.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: This is required regardless of whether salary is charged to the project. Commons ID for postdocs is required for RPPRs; for undergraduate and graduate students, Commons ID is required with RPPRs. Graduate Student and Postdoctoral roles should NOT be used for individuals submitting Individual Fellowships (use PD/PI) nor for trainees on institutional training grants reported via xTrain (use Trainee Role).

rubrics_metrics.name: Required Commons ID at time of submission for certain roles
rubrics_metrics.description: A Commons ID is required at time of submission for sponsors in fellowship applications, component leads on multi-project applications, primary mentors on career development applications, and all individuals listed on the R&R Senior/Key Person Profile (Expanded) Form (applies to Senior/Key Personnel and Other Significant Contributors).
rubrics_metrics.guidance: For other roles Commons ID is strongly encouraged but currently optional; a general Project Personnel role exists for those not assigned other Commons Roles.

rubrics_metrics.name: eRA Commons functional role — post-submission primary use
rubrics_metrics.description: The eRA Commons is the primary site post-submission for accessing grant information (IC assignments, review outcomes, Summary Statements, Notices of Award) and performing business processes (Internet Assisted Review, Just-In-Time, RPPRs, notification of extensions without funds, Closeout documents).
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Appropriate user roles are assigned based on responsibilities; institutional/organizational officials maintain Institutional Profile after registration.
